Simulate Time-to-Event Data

Source: R/simtte.R
sim_tte.Rd

Main function of simtte. Simulates a time-to-event dataset (survival dataset) using either a Weibull parametric model or an M-spline flexible baseline hazard model. Event times are generated via inverse transform sampling from the cumulative hazard function computed by mrgsolve.

Usage

sim_tte(
  pi,
  log_pi = TRUE,
  mu = -3,
  coefs = 0,
  basis = NULL,
  time = seq(0, 100, by = 1),
  end_time,
  type = "weibull",
  event_time_method = c("grid", "log_survival"),
  lp_data = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

pi

Numeric matrix or vector. Prognostic index (linear predictor) for each individual. Given a covariate matrix X and coefficient vector b, pi = X %*% b. Must be non-empty and finite (no NA/NaN/Inf/-Inf).

log_pi

Logical; is the prognostic index already on the log scale? Default TRUE.

mu

Numeric scalar. Intercept parameter of the model. Must be finite. Default -3.

coefs

Numeric vector. For M-spline models, the coefficients of each spline basis function. For Weibull models, the shape parameter (scalar), which must be strictly positive. Must be finite in all cases.

basis

Numeric matrix. Basis matrix for M-spline models, with one row per element of time and one column per coefficient in coefs. Must be finite. Ignored for Weibull models. Default NULL.

time

Numeric vector. The output time grid: the exact set of times at which the survival trajectory is simulated and reported, and therefore the set of times at which an event can be detected (see "Time grid and event-time resolution" below). For M-spline models, time must additionally be sorted in non-decreasing order and have one element per row of basis (the baseline hazard is only defined at these points). Must be non-negative, finite, and contain no NA/NaN. Default seq(0, 100, by = 1).

end_time

Numeric scalar. Administrative censoring horizon. Defaults to max(time). Any requested time points beyond end_time are dropped, and end_time itself is always added to the output grid so that censoring lands exactly on it. Must be non-negative; end_time = 0 is accepted (a degenerate zero-duration follow-up: the output grid is just time 0, and since \(S(0) = 1\) for every supported model, every subject is censored at 0). For Weibull models end_time may otherwise be any non-negative value, including below min(time) or above max(time) (the closed-form hazard is defined for all t >= 0). For M-spline models end_time must satisfy min(time) <= end_time <= max(time): the baseline hazard is only defined on the supplied time grid and this package does not extrapolate it in either direction.

type

Character string. Model type: "weibull" or "ms" (M-splines). Default "weibull".

event_time_method

Character string. "grid" (default) or "log_survival". See "Event-time interpolation" below. Forwarded explicitly to sim_tte_df; it is unrelated to the mrgsolve simulation step and is never passed via ....

lp_data

NULL (default) or a data frame with columns time, lp, and optionally ID, giving a time-varying linear predictor lp(t) for the built-in Weibull/M-spline models. See "Time-varying lp(t)" below. NULL preserves every prior behavior of sim_tte() byte-for-byte.

...

Additional arguments passed to mrgsim. tgrid, obsonly, nocb, carry_out/carry.out, and data are controlled internally to guarantee the contracts documented here and cannot be overridden; supplying them raises an error naming the argument.

Value

A data frame with columns:

sim_time

Simulated event or censoring time.

sim_status

Event indicator (1 = event, 0 = censored).

ID

Subject identifier.

lp

Log prognostic index (linear predictor).

Time grid and event-time resolution

The output grid used for simulation is sort(unique(time)), restricted to values <= end_time, with end_time appended if it is not already present. mrgsolve is instructed to report the survival trajectory only at these times (via its tgrid mechanism), so the grid is deterministic and is not silently replaced by mrgsolve's own default output schedule.

Event times are then resolved by sim_tte_df as the first grid point at which the survival probability falls to or below a uniform random draw. For event_time_method = "grid" (the default), no interpolation between grid points is performed: the resolution of the simulated event time is exactly the spacing of time. For event_time_method = "log_survival", a crossing that falls strictly between two grid points is refined by interpolation; see "Event-time interpolation" below and the corresponding section of sim_tte_df for the full mathematical contract (this is the function sim_tte() delegates to internally, forwarding event_time_method explicitly). A subject whose survival never crosses the threshold on the grid is censored at end_time under either method.

Event-time interpolation

See the "Event-time interpolation" section of sim_tte_df for the full mathematical contract and edge-case rules; sim_tte() simply forwards event_time_method to it. In summary: "log_survival" assumes the hazard is constant between consecutive reported trajectory points and linearly interpolates cumulative hazard accordingly. For the M-spline model this recovers the event time implied by the discretized (piecewise-constant, via the "M-spline hazard carry convention" below) hazard exactly. For the Weibull model with shape != 1, whose true hazard is not constant within an interval, it is an approximation whose accuracy improves as time is refined (exact when shape == 1, the one case where the Weibull hazard genuinely is constant).

M-spline hazard carry convention

For type = "ms", basis %*% coefs gives a baseline hazard value at each element of time; this is supplied to mrgsolve as a time-varying input, not evaluated as a continuous spline function at arbitrary times. The package fixes the piecewise interpretation explicitly (mrgsolve's nocb = FALSE, i.e. last-observation-carried-forward): the hazard value reported at time[i] applies from time[i] (inclusive) until time[i + 1] (exclusive) – a right-continuous step function in the hazard. Concretely, for knots/hazards time = c(0, 1, 2), basehaz = c(1, 2, 4): \(S(0.5) = \exp(-0.5)\), \(S(1) = \exp(-1)\), \(S(1.5) = \exp(-2)\), \(S(2) = \exp(-3)\) (verified directly against mrgsolve output; this is not the mrgsolve default, which is next-observation-carried-backward and would instead give \(S(0.5) = \exp(-1)\)).

A consequence of this convention: the hazard value associated with the last element of time has no interval after it to apply to, so it never affects the survival trajectory (it would only matter if end_time extended past max(time), which is not permitted; see end_time above). basis/coefs therefore define length(time) - 1 active piecewise-constant hazard segments, not length(time).

This is a grid-based piecewise-constant hazard, not continuous M-spline evaluation: the package receives precomputed basis values at specific times and never re-evaluates the spline basis at arbitrary times.

Time-varying lp(t)

Supplying lp_data allows the linear predictor itself to vary over time, for both built-in models. lp_data must contain time (finite, non-negative) and lp (finite; unlike a hazard, negative values are valid) columns, and, optionally, an ID column:

  • no ID: a single population-level \(lp(t)\) trajectory, applied identically to every subject;

  • ID present: subject-specific trajectories. sort(unique(lp_data$ID)) must equal 1:length(pi) exactly (one full trajectory per subject; no partial coverage).

In both cases, pi keeps its existing role as each subject's baseline linear-predictor offset: \(lp_{\mathrm{effective}}(t) = pi_i + lp(t)\). lp_data rows are not sorted or deduplicated automatically (same philosophy as sim_tte_df's trajectory contract): unsorted times are an error; duplicate times are accepted only with an identical lp value, otherwise an error. lp(t) is piecewise constant under last-observation-carried-forward (the same convention as basehaz, above): the value at lp_data$time[i] applies from that time until the next lp_data knot for that subject. lp_data's own time grid is independent of, and need not coincide with, the main time argument.

Coverage requirement: every subject's lp_data must include an observation at time = 0 (there is no implicit \(lp(0)\)). For M-spline models, which cannot extrapolate, it must additionally reach at least end_time; for Weibull models this is not required, since the last known lp value is carried forward for any remaining follow-up.

For type = "weibull", a separate, distinct model (weibull_tv) is used internally whenever lp_data is supplied; the constant-lp closed-form Weibull model (inst/models/weibull.cpp) used whenever lp_data is NULL is not modified or replaced. weibull_tv computes \(S(t)\) by an exact closed-form cumulative-hazard summation over the piecewise-constant \(lp(t)\) segments – it does not use ODE integration or internal-solver event detection (the latter was investigated and rejected; see PHASE_E_THRESHOLD_TRACKING_REPORT.md) – so it retains the same solver-free numerical robustness established for the baseline model. For type = "ms", the existing basehaz(t) mechanism and lp(t) combine as \(h(t) = basehaz(t) \exp[\mu + lp(t)]\), both under the same last-observation-carried-forward convention.

References

Bender R, Augustin T, Blettner M (2005). Generating survival times to simulate Cox proportional hazards models. Statistics in Medicine, 24(11), 1713–1723. doi:10.1002/sim.2059

Royston P, Parmar MKB (2002). Flexible parametric proportional-hazards and proportional-odds models for censored survival data, with application to prognostic modelling and estimation of treatment effects. Statistics in Medicine, 21(15), 2175–2197. doi:10.1002/sim.1203

See also

sim_tte_df, which turns any (ID, time, p11) trajectory, including one from your own mrgsolve model, into event times. sim_tte_ode, for joint PK/PD and time-to-event simulation with in-solver event detection (also the route for Cox-model data; see its "Simulating from a Cox model" section). add_censoring, to add independent right censoring to this function's output (call it directly on the returned data frame; there is no argument here for it), then add_interval_censoring, to map the result onto an assessment-time interval. explore_pi_tq_surv, to see how the prognostic index moves survival before simulating.

Examples

# Fast Weibull example with a small dataset
set.seed(1)
lp <- matrix(rnorm(5, 0, 0.5), nrow = 5)
result <- sim_tte(
  pi = lp, mu = -1, coefs = 1.1,
  time = seq(0.1, 10, by = 0.5),
  type = "weibull", end_time = 10
)
#> Loading model from cache.
head(result)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>   sim_time sim_status    ID      lp
#>      <dbl>      <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1      5.1          1     1 -0.313 
#> 2      4.1          1     2  0.0918
#> 3      1.6          1     3 -0.418 
#> 4      1.6          1     4  0.798 
#> 5      1.1          1     5  0.165 
# \donttest{
# Larger examples using bundled ms_data
data("ms_data")
mu <- ms_data$mu
basis <- ms_data$basis
coefs <- ms_data$coefs
time <- ms_data$time
lp <- matrix(runif(nrow(basis)), nrow = nrow(basis))
wei_sim <- sim_tte(pi = lp, mu = -1, coefs = 1.1,
  time = time, type = "weibull", end_time = 100)
#> Loading model from cache.
ms_sim <- sim_tte(pi = lp, mu = mu, basis = basis,
  coefs = coefs, time = time, type = "ms")
#> Building ms ... 
#> done.
# }
